blocks.text:
I'm trying to estimate how buried Ser118 is by checking its side chain coordinates against nearby residues, starting with distances to Arg34's side chain atoms in this helical bundle structure.

The OG atom appears to sit roughly 3.3-4.5 Å from R34's CD/NE/CG/CB atoms, suggesting the two side chains face each other. I'm continuing to scan other nearby residues—L122, K119, L26, Y115—to see which ones fall within a plausible burial radius of S118's side chain.

This narrows the contacts to R34's guanidinium group, K119's backbone/CB, and Y115's ring, which fits with S118 sitting on a helix face pointed into the bundle. I'm now considering the helical wheel pattern of the segment L113-L122 to figure out which residues line up on the same face as S118.

The CB-to-OG vector points roughly toward -y and -z, in the direction of R34, confirming the side chain is oriented into that region. I want to check if GLN28's side chain also sits nearby to complete the local contact picture.

Checking K119's side chain against S118's OG shows it's about 4.3 Å away, so S118 does seem somewhat enclosed. Rather than continuing residue-by-residue, I think a more efficient approach is counting heavy atoms within 8-10 Å of the CB to gauge burial, comparing residues by proximity to that reference point.

Continuing through the residue distance calculations, I'm checking F30, A24, V50, L63, L76, Q77, I80, A117, and K119 against the reference point, finding most are far except A117 which comes in around 4.9 Å.

I'm also computing distances for L120, V121, L122, Y115, F114, F116, and A112, with several falling in the 4.6-7.2 Å range from the target position.

Compiling the local neighborhood, I see it's dominated by the helical stretch (114-122) plus I31, R34, F30, and A35. Now I'm thinking about whether the OG atom is solvent-accessible, given serine's small side chain and reference SASA value of around 118 Å².

I'm checking the backbone atoms of S118 for exposure, noting the carbonyl oxygen hydrogen-bonds to K123's nitrogen as part of the helix, and confirming that its packing partners are I31, R34, F30, and A35 since F114-A117 belong to the same helix. Now I'm measuring the CB-CB distance between S118 and I31.

The distances between S118's CB and I31's various side chain atoms all fall in the 4-5 Å range, confirming a solid packing contact with I31's side chain, while OG of S118 reaches toward R34. F30 is farther out at around 6.3 Å, so S118's side chain appears to nestle between the helix and this region around residues 27-37.

Checking whether this pocket is solvent-exposed, I trace R34's side chain path from CB through CG, CD, NE, CZ, to NH2 — it curves right into the same region as OG, meaning R34's aliphatic chain, along with I31 and likely Y115's ring and K119, surrounds and shields OG from solvent.

I'm scanning for other nearby residues that could open a cavity, checking distances from OG to ASP71 and GLN77 (both too far, 7+ Å), and noting this structure only covers residues 10-37 and 49-167, missing 38-48, which could affect the picture. I'm now tallying all atoms within 7 Å of OG to get a clearer sense of how buried it actually is.

R34 alone contributes about nine atoms within that radius through its CZ, NH1, NH2, CA, C, and N positions. Now I'm checking ILE31's side chain atoms (CB, CG1, CG2) to see how much further coverage they add.

Moving on to Y115, I'm working through its ring atoms - CB, CG, CD1, CD2, CE1, CE2 - computing each distance to see which fall within the cutoff.

Then I hit something notable: OG to Y115's backbone O comes out to 2.90 Å, which is right in hydrogen-bonding range. Let me double-check that calculation to confirm it's a real H-bond contact.

This confirms a classic serine helix-capping interaction, with OG hydrogen-bonded to the i-3 backbone carbonyl. I'm now scanning nearby residues F116 and A117, computing distances from OG to their CB, CA, N, and C atoms to see if any other contacts fall within range.

Continuing to K119, I'm checking distances from OG to its backbone N, CA, CB, CG, and CD atoms, finding several in the 4 Å neighborhood range worth noting.

Then I'm calculating CE and NZ distances, both falling above 5.4 Å, before moving to L122's CG and CD1 measurements, and finally starting F30's CB, CG, and CD2 distance checks.

Given how many atoms cluster around this residue, S118's OG sits in a tightly packed pocket surrounded by F30, Y115, I31, R34, K119, and L122, with essentially every direction accounted for — this points strongly toward a buried position with low overall solvent accessibility, though the backbone itself might retain some exposure.

I'm checking whether anything occupies that +x pocket near (-3.5,-2.5,2) — ILE31 CB and GLN32 CA are nearby but at different z-levels, so this might just be an open channel rather than a filled cavity.

Testing a water probe shifted to (-4.5,-2.7,1.6): distances to L122 CD1 (~3.35Å), I31 CG2 (~4.4Å), L122 CG (~3.7Å), and V121 CB all clear the minimum contact radius, so this spot looks feasible.

But S118 CB comes out to just 2.15Å from that point, which is too close for a probe—so the channel is narrower than I thought. Given how many neighbors surround this residue (F30, Y115, I31, R34, F116), this really does look like a buried core position rather than solvent-exposed, though I should still sanity-check the SASA estimate given Ser's small max side-chain area.

Since the CB clearly faces I31 and F30 rather than solvent, and the backbone O is H-bonded to K122's amide N, this position's relative SASA is likely under 0.1 — I'll call it buried.
